author: Elastic
attributes.description: This rule detects the registration of a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner by a user and source ASN (autonomous system) pair not seen in the last 5 days. The source IP is resolved to its ASN at query time, so address churn inside the same ISP or cloud provider does not produce new alerts. Adversaries may abuse self-hosted runners to execute workflow jobs on customer infrastructure.
attributes.name: New GitHub Self Hosted Action Runner
attributes.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating New GitHub Self Hosted Action Runner

Adversaries who gain the ability to modify or trigger workflows in a linked GitHub repository can execute arbitrary commands on the runner host.

### Possible investigation steps

- Validate the user is authoried to perform this change
- Review the purpose of the self-hosted action runner and what actions will be executed.
- Verify if there is any adjascent  sensitive file access or collection.
- Correlate with other alerts and investiguate if this activity is related to a supply chain attack.

### False positive analysis

- Authorized github self-hosted actions runner.

### Response and remediation

- Immediately isolate the affected system from the network to prevent further unauthorized command execution and potential lateral movement.
- Terminate any suspicious child processes that were initiated by the Github actions runner.
- Conduct a thorough review of the affected system's logs and configurations to identify any unauthorized changes or additional indicators of compromise.
- Restore the system from a known good backup if any unauthorized changes or malicious activities are confirmed.
- Implement application whitelisting to prevent unauthorized execution.
- Escalate the incident to the security operations center (SOC) or incident response team for further investigation and to assess the potential impact on the broader network.
attributes.query:
FROM logs-github.audit-*
| WHERE event.dataset == "github.audit" AND event.category == "configuration"
  AND event.action IN ("repo.register_self_hosted_runner", "org.register_self_hosted_runner", "enterprise.register_self_hosted_runner")
  AND user.name IS NOT NULL AND github.actor_ip IS NOT NULL
| IP_LOCATION asn = github.actor_ip WITH { "database_file": "GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb", "properties": ["asn", "organization_name"] }
| IP_LOCATION geo = github.actor_ip WITH { "properties": ["country_iso_code"] }
| WHERE asn.asn IS NOT NULL
| STATS Esql.event_count = COUNT(*),
        Esql.first_seen = MIN(@timestamp),
        Esql.last_seen = MAX(@timestamp),
        Esql.ip_values = VALUES(github.actor_ip),
        Esql.event_action_values = VALUES(event.action),
        Esql.repo_values = VALUES(github.repo),
        Esql.org_values = VALUES(github.org),
        Esql.country_values = VALUES(geo.country_iso_code),
        Esql.user_agent_values = VALUES(github.user_agent)
  BY user.name, asn.asn, asn.organization_name
// The 5-day history is the rule look-back (from = now-7205m). A user/ASN pair is new when its first
// event falls inside the current interval; the 10m bound allows for the 5m interval plus scheduling drift.
| WHERE DATE_DIFF("minute", Esql.first_seen, NOW()) <= 10
| EVAL Esql.source_as_number = asn.asn, Esql.source_as_organization_name = asn.organization_name
| KEEP user.name, Esql.*
